localised_to_the_instruction.method: decode the program body and find the issue positions of the EMBED_LOOKUP descriptors, then read the body range of every loop descriptor
localised_to_the_instruction.the_defect: NO LOOP IN THE DEPLOYMENT COVERS PROGRAM POSITION 6.  The loops around it are 1085 (body 4..5), 1101 (body 8..9) and 1075 (body 11..237), so positions 6..7 are a gap with no loop open.  Descriptor 1100 is issued into that gap while its output view carries a LOOP_INDUCTION term naming loop 1076, whose body is 239..495.  The tight loop this operator needs was never emitted, and the term points at an unrelated structural loop.
localised_to_the_instruction.the_pattern: every EMBED_LOOKUP that resolves is wrapped in a TIGHT single-instruction loop: 1093 issues at position 4 and its loop 1085 has body 4..5; the rank-3 pair have bodies 256..257 and 2103..2104.  Descriptor 1100 issues at position 6 and should therefore have a loop with body 6..7.
localised_to_the_instruction.why_i_have_not_patched_it: the fix is in the ROM program builder's loop-scope emission, which is shared by every ROM product.  The three DeepSeek-V4-Flash cells and the Qwen3 ROM cells close through that same code, and they are the matrix's main asset.  A blind edit there can break six closed cells to chase three open ones, so the localisation is recorded to the instruction and the change is left to be made against the emitter with the V4-Flash and Qwen3 walks as regression gates.

reduced_versus_shipped.the_anomaly: every EMBED_LOOKUP in the working reduced deployment sits 5 to 8 descriptors after the loop that indexes its output.  In BOTH shipped deployments the second one sits 24 back, and the loop it names (1076) is EARLIER than the loop the FIRST EMBED_LOOKUP uses (1085) -- a later operator reaching back past an intervening loop.  Loop 1076 closes at program position 495, so if descriptor 1100 issues after that the loop is gone, which is exactly what the resolver reports.
reduced_versus_shipped.the_question_for_whoever_fixes_it: a single-iteration loop (bounds [0,1), max_iterations 1) around an embedding lookup is the shape a loop that should have been folded away leaves behind.  So either loop 1076 should not exist and the view should carry no dynamic term, or descriptor 1100 belongs inside its body.  The reduced deployment answers neither question because its pairing is already consistent.
reduced_versus_shipped.what: every TENSOR.EMBED_LOOKUP in each deployment, with the loop its output view is indexed by

the_refusal.failure: prefill failed: view 1097: loop 1076 is not active

localised_to.prior_art_in_this_tree: EMBED_LOOKUP has a recorded history of addressing faults here: "legacy unkeyed bases ignore the placement table -- EMBED_LOOKUP and GATHER addressed by launch counter, so the token id was validated and never used". That is a different fault from this one, but it is the same operator and the same part of the lowering.
localised_to.reading: the EMBED_LOOKUP at descriptor 1100 writes a rank-2 view whose only dynamic term is loop 1076, a SINGLE-ITERATION loop whose body spans program positions 239 to 495.  For the view to resolve, the operator must be issued inside that body.  It is not, so the resolver refuses.  Exactly one descriptor in the deployment references view 1097, so there is no ambiguity about which operator owns the fault.

the_refusal.what_it_means: view 1097 carries a dynamic term of kind LOOP_INDUCTION naming loop 1076, and loop 1076 is not in the active loop set when the view is resolved. The view is used outside the loop that indexes it -- a lowering fault in the deployment, caught by the resolver rather than producing a wrong address.
